newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks slide at open after Dow dips.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks slide at open after Dow dips.

text.p: The Australian share market opened lower on Monday with a softer U.S. market weighing it down as it resumed after the ANZAC day long weekend.

Investor interest remained low with turnover figures inflated by the exercise of April series options belying a slow start. Pre-opening trades relating to options exercises totalled A$773 million (US$595 million).
The All Ordinaries index lost 13.5 points to 2,461.2.

"I'm not expecting much of anything today after option exercises on Thursday," said a dealer at a Brisbane-based brokerage, pointing to several day's softness in U.S. markets that a hesitant local market had to absorb.
"U.S. markets are a bit softer and the bond futures are trading down a bit but it looks not much will happen at all."

Bank sector leader National Australia Bank topped turnover early with 25.2 million shares traded, over 24 million of them in option exercises put through before the market opened. National Australia Bank shares lost two to A$17.05.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about nine to five, while about 40 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
